رَجْمَةٌ : see رَجَمٌ, second sentence. ―
-b2- [It is applied in the present day to Any heap of stones thrown together or piled up.] ―
-b3- Also A [kind of turret, such as is called] مَنَارَة, like a بَيْت [i. e. tent, or house, &c.], around which they used to circuit: a poet says, “↓ كَمَا طَافَ بِالرَّجْمَةِ المُرْتَجِمْ
” [Like as when he who beat the ground circuited around the رجمة]. (TA.) ―
-b4- رجمة [thus written, but perhaps it is ↓ رُجْمَةٌ ,] is also sing. of رِجَام signifying [Hills, or mountains, &c., such as are called] هِضَاب [pl. of هَضْبَةٌ]. (AA, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
